scenes.title: All safe, all well
scenes.narration: It took four tries to reach Elephant Island through the ice. On August 30th, 1916, a small Chilean steamer, the Yelcho, came into the bay. Shackleton counted the figures on the beach. Twenty-two. All safe. All well.

scenes.title: How they survived
scenes.narration: People ask me how they did it. I think it was this. Their leader never let a single man believe it was over. Not on the ice. Not in the boats. Not for one day.

scenes.title: Endurance
scenes.narration: I stayed in the whaling trade for thirty more years. Whenever a hard winter came, I'd think of twenty-eight men on the ice and one word. Endurance.

scenes.title: Subscribe
scenes.narration: If you've stayed with me this far, I think this story stayed with you too. If it did, leave a like and subscribe. That's how I know you want more stories like this one, and it helps them reach more people.

scenes.title: What comes next
scenes.narration: In 1897, a hundred thousand men set out for the Klondike gold fields in the Yukon. To get there, they had to haul a ton of supplies over a frozen mountain pass. Most never found any gold. That story is next.
